title: Missing Number In Arithmetic Progression
summary: Given an array where the difference between consecutive elements is constant, and one value is missing (not the first or last), return the missing value.
statement: Given an array where the difference between consecutive elements is constant, and one value is missing (not the first or last), return the missing value.
constraints: 3 <= len(arr) <= 1000; arr is an arithmetic progression with one interior value removed.
The progression may increase, decrease, or be constant.
hints: The original progression has len(arr)+1 terms, so its step is (last-first)/len(arr).
Scan adjacent values for the one gap that differs from the step.
Return left+step at that gap; constant progressions return their repeated value.
All intact gaps equal the true step, while the removed interior term doubles exactly one gap.
editorial: All intact gaps equal the true step, while the removed interior term doubles exactly one gap.

tests.explanation: The common difference is two, so nine is missing between seven and eleven.
The descending progression has step -1 and is missing fourteen.
